media.titulo_original: #27006 — Keyboard shortcuts not forwarding to IDE from TeamCode terminal
media.titulo_traduzido: (#27006) atalhos do teclado nao estao sendo encaminhados para a IDE a partir do terminal do TeamCode
media.descricao_original:
### Description

Several regressions when using  inside IDE integrated terminals (Cursor, Windsurf):

1. Keyboard shortcuts are no longer forwarding from the  terminal to the IDE. For example, Cmd+Option+K no longer inserts the current file path or highlighted text — it only works if focus is on the editor first. Shortcuts like Ctrl+Shift+G (git sidebar) and Cmd+Shift+E (file bar) also don't forward.

2. The workaround from the original ticket — renaming the integrated terminal tab  so it receives the Cmd+Option+K autofill — is still required. This should work out of the box without manual renaming. But this is only for while focus is already in IDE, not while in integrated terminal

media.titulo_original: #27700 — Grep/Glob tools hang and block other sessions with concurrent usage
media.titulo_traduzido: (#27700) grep/Glob tools hang and block other sessions with concurrent usage
media.descricao_original:
I'm using OpenCode Desktop v1.15.0 on macOS (Apple Silicon).

I had two TUI sessions open on the same project (a Git repo). In session A, I asked the agent to search for something using grep. While that was still running, I switched to session B and asked it to do another grep search on the same project.

Session B's grep tool never returned. It just stayed spinning. I switched back to session A — that one was also frozen now. I had to Ctrl+C out of both sessions and restart the sidecar.

I expected the two sessions to work independently. Searching in one session shouldn't block searches in another.

Steps I can reproduce:
1. Open two (or more) TUI sessions on the same Git repo
2. In session A, trigger a multi-file grep search (e.g. "search for all usages of X")
3. While it's running, switch to session B and trigger another grep search
4. Session B's tool call hangs. Switching back to session A, it's also frozen.
5. Only Ctrl+C recovers.

I also noticed this happens more often when Cod

1. Log in to OpenCode with an account that has a ChatGPT Plus (OpenAI) subscription

3. OpenCode shows error: "Method of billing not enabled" or similar
4. When trying to configure the billing method, OpenCode requires paying 8/month (Black plan) or using Zen Credits

## Expected Behavior

Being able to use my existing OpenAI (ChatGPT Plus) subscription directly in OpenCode without having to additionally pay OpenCode.

## Actual Behavior

- OpenCode requires its own billing method
- Forces paying 8/month or loading 0 in credits
- Does not properly use the user's OpenAI subscription

## Additional Information

- I have an active ChatGPT Plus subscription (I regularly bill from OpenAI)
- I have connected my Ope

1. Make a request to the OpenCode server with `Accept-Encoding: zstd, gzip`
2. Observe the response uses gzip, not zstd

### Expected behavior

The server should negotiate zstd as the preferred encoding when the client supports it, falling back to gzip/deflate.

### System info

- OpenCode version: v1.15.3
- OS: Linux

baixa.titulo_original: #27276 — [Bug] Git diff shows unmodified files as "Modified" on Windows (CRLF + symlink type changes)
baixa.titulo_traduzido: (#27276) [Bug] Git diff mostra arquivos nao modificados como "Modificado" no Windows (CRLF + alteracoes de tipo de link simbolico)
baixa.descricao_original:
### Description

### Describe the bug
On Windows, the Review window and Changes tab show many files as "Modified"
even though they have no actual content changes. Two root causes:
1. CRLF/LF line ending mismatch — All text files appear modified because
   the git layer overrides core.autocrlf to false on a system where it
   defaults to true, causing every text file's CRLF working tree to
   differ from LF in the repo.
2. Symlink type changes — There are 62 symlink files in the repository.
   Windows does not natively support symlinks, so they are checked out
   as regular files. The git layer forces core.symlinks=true, causing
   git diff to detect type changes (T) for all of them.
### To Reproduce
1. Clone the repo on Windows (where core.autocrlf defaults to true)
2. Open the Review window (VCS diff mode) in the Desktop app
3. Observe that all text files and all symlink files appear as "Modified"
### Expected behavior
Only files with actual content changes should appear as "Modified"

baixa.titulo_original: #27476 — PowerShell Chinese encoding + docx read + grep download + Word COM issues on Windows
baixa.titulo_traduzido: (#27476) powerShell Chinese encoding + docx read + grep download + Word COM issues on Windows
baixa.descricao_original:
## Description

On Windows 11, OpenCode encountered several toolchain issues when asked to process .docx files (read and write) and handle non-ASCII text through PowerShell:

### 1. Read tool: cannot handle .docx files
`Read` returns `Cannot read binary file` for .docx (ZIP+XML). This is a very common format for documents.

### 2. Grep tool: transport error downloading ripgrep
```
Transport error (GET https://github.com/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/download/...)
```
Prevents file content search when ripgrep is not yet installed.

### 3. PowerShell `$var:` syntax causes ParserError
When writing PowerShell scripts, patterns like `"[$file:$lineNum] $line"` trigger:
```
Variable reference is not valid. ':' was not followed by a valid variable name character.
```
Generated code snippets should use `${file}` to be safe.

### 4. PowerShell console garbles non-ASCII characters
Chinese characters output via Write-Host appear as mojibake, requiring workarounds (write to file, then Read).

### 5.

baixa.titulo_original: #22215 — fix: WSL UNC paths break bash and git on Windows
baixa.titulo_traduzido: (#22215) fix: WSL UNC paths break bash and git on Windows
baixa.descricao_original:
## Bug

On Windows, when the project directory is accessed via a UNC path (`\\wsl$\...`), tools like bash, file search, and git all break because Windows-native path handling doesn't understand UNC paths.

## Details

Many Windows developers work inside WSL for toolchain access while opencode runs natively on Windows. When the project lives in WSL, the path comes through as `\\wsl$\distro\mnt\c\...` which no native Windows tool can handle.

## Suggested Fix

Detect UNC paths and translate to WSL equivalents, run git/shell commands through `wsl.exe`, translate results back.

baixa.titulo_original: #22799 — Windows: project-local drive-less paths fail tool boundary checks
baixa.titulo_traduzido: (#22799) windows: project-local drive-less paths fail tool boundary checks
baixa.descricao_original:
### Description

On Windows, project-local paths that lose their drive letter at tool boundaries can be handled inconsistently.

A path like `C:\repo\src\file.ts` can arrive as `/repo/src/file.ts` or `\\repo\\src\\file.ts` and be treated as external or outside the project even though it is on the current drive and inside the repo. This affects real tool boundaries such as `read`, `write`, `edit`, `lsp`, and `external_directory` checks.

The same investigation also exposed a file-backed plugin/theme metadata problem on Windows: if the file contents change without the mtime changing, refresh/install can keep using stale metadata.

### Plugins

None required for the path bug.

### OpenCode version

dev at `c8af8f96c` during investigation. Fix branch: `fix/windows-plugin-loader-ci` (`57518bd9b`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, start in a project directory.
2. Pass a project-local file through a tool boundary using a drive-less rooted path form such as `/repo/src/file.ts`.
3. Obser

## Summary

Every opencode session startup logs a single `ERROR e=RipgrepExtractionFailedError` within ~200ms of startup, **even though**:

alta.titulo_original: #23663 — [BUG] Custom LSP servers always send languageId: 'plaintext', causing servers like Godot LSP to fail
alta.titulo_traduzido: (#23663) [Bug] Custom LSP servers always send languageId: 'plaintext', causing servers like Godot LSP to fail
alta.descricao_original:
## Description

When using a **custom LSP server** (e.g., `godot-lsp-bridge` for GDScript), OpenCode always sends `languageId: "plaintext"` in the `textDocument/didOpen` notification, regardless of the file extension configured in `lsp.extensions`.

This causes language servers that rely on `languageId` (like Godot's LSP server) to **not send diagnostics**, because they only recognize their specific language ID (e.g., `gdscript`).

### Root Cause

In `packages/opencode/src/lsp/client.ts` line 148:

```typescript
const languageId = LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS[extension] ?? "plaintext"
```

OpenCode uses a hardcoded `LANGUAGE_EXTENSIONS` mapping table for built-in LSP servers. For any extension **not** in this table (including custom LSP extensions like `.gd`), it falls back to `"plaintext"`.

The `lsp.*.extensions` configuration is only used to **match** which LSP server to start, but is **not** used to determine the `languageId` sent to the server.

## Plugins

oh-my-openagent
godot-lsp-bridge

alta.titulo_original: #23695 — Plugin config does not support tilde (~/) paths
alta.titulo_traduzido: (#23695) plugin config does not support tilde (~/) paths
alta.descricao_original:
## Description

When configuring a plugin using a tilde path (e.g. `~/my-plugin`), opencode fails to load it.

## Steps to Reproduce

Add a plugin in `opencode.json` using a `~/` path:

```json
{
  "plugin": ["~/my-local-plugin"]
}
```

## Expected Behavior

`~/my-local-plugin` is resolved to the user's home directory and loaded as a local plugin.

## Actual Behavior

The path is not recognized as a local path specifier. It gets passed to npm resolution and fails.

## Root Cause

`isPathPluginSpec()` in `plugin/shared.ts` only recognizes `file://`, `.`-prefixed, and absolute paths. `~/` is not handled.

## Summary

Tool calling fails in OpenCode for xAI models via OpenRouter because emitted tool/input JSON schemas include `additionalProperties: false`, which xAI rejects.

## Repro

Model:
- `openrouter/x-ai/grok-4.1-fast`

Observed error:
- `[xAI] Invalid request content: Schema validation failed: [standard_violation] /properties/properties/additionalProperties: property schema 'false' is not supported`

## Notes

This happens on the native OpenCode OpenRouter path, not from external plugins.

OpenCode currently runs tool schemas through `ProviderTransform.schema(...)` before handing them to the model. For xAI via OpenRouter, that transform should strip `additionalProperties: false` recursively.

## Why this is safe

xAI structured output docs state:
- `additionalProperties` defaults to `false`
- schemas with boolean property schemas like `false` are rejected

So omitting explicit `additionalProperties: false` preserves behavior while avoiding the xAI validator error.

## Proposed fix

alta.titulo_original: #23782 — fix(tui): cannot navigate into grandchild sessions from subagent view
alta.titulo_traduzido: (#23782) fix(tui): cannot navigate into grandchild sessions from subagent view
alta.descricao_original:
### Description

In the TUI session tree, when a sub-agent spawns its own child (grandchild session), pressing down or clicking to navigate into the grandchild session does nothing. Navigation into child sessions only works from the root session level.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a session that spawns a sub-agent
2. Navigate into the sub-agent session (this works)
3. The sub-agent spawns its own child session (grandchild)
4. Press down / try to navigate into the grandchild → nothing happens

### What's happening

`moveFirstChild()` and `moveChild()` in `session/index.tsx` use `children()` to look up sessions, but `children()` only returns the root session's direct children. From a sub-agent context, the grandchild sessions are not in that list, so navigation fails silently.

### OpenCode version

v1.14.x (dev)

### Operating System

macOS

### Terminal

Any

With an `eslint` dependency in the project, opencode's TUI reports the ESLint LSP as loaded but the agent never sees any ESLint diagnostics — even ones that `mise run lint` and the VS Code `dbaeumer.vscode-eslint` extension both report on the same file. Investigation revealed two distinct bugs. The second is the blocker: opencode's LSP client does not implement LSP 3.17 pull-model diagnostics, which is the only mode the current `vscode-eslint` server (v3.x) uses.

## Ambiente

- opencode: `1.14.20` (from `/devvol/data/mise/installs/github-anomalyco-opencode/1.14.20/opencode`)
- Node: `24.15.0`
- OS: Linux (devcontainer)
- Project has `eslint` as a peer dependency and uses ESLint flat config with `@typescript-eslint/prefer-readonly-parameter-types` enabled.
- Visible in VS Code and `mise run lint`: `src/bin/cli.ts:19:18 warning Parameter should be a read only type (@typescript-eslint/prefer-readonly-parameter-types)`.

agent anyway — but **all frontmatter is silently discarded**. The agent loads

alta.titulo_original: #24328 — [BUG] Lock operations lack timeout/eviction; concurrency issues in acp/session and session/run-state
alta.titulo_traduzido: (#24328) [Bug] Lock operations lack timeout/eviction; concurrency issues in acp/session and session/run-state
alta.descricao_original:
## Description

Four concurrency improvements:

1. **src/util/lock.ts** — Lock operations have no timeout. A stuck lock holder blocks all waiters forever. No deadlock detection.

2. **src/tool/edit.ts** — `locks` Map grows unbounded per unique file path. No eviction mechanism.

3. **src/acp/session.ts** — `setModel`/`setVariant`/`setMode` do read-then-Map.set() on the same object reference already stored in the Map. The redundant `.set()` creates an illusion of atomic update.

4. **src/session/run-state.ts** — `runners.delete()` + `runners.get()` in the onIdle callback are separate operations, not atomic within cooperatively-scheduled Effect fibers.

### Reproduction steps

1. Inspect `src/util/lock.ts` — note no timeout parameter exists on `read()` or `write()` lock operations
2. Inspect `src/tool/edit.ts:35` — note the `locks` Map has no eviction logic
3. Inspect `src/acp/session.ts` — note `this.sessions.set(sessionId, session)` after mutating the object already in the Map
4. Inspec

alta.titulo_original: #27697 — Regression in v1.14.50: `TeamCode run --format json` drops post-tool-call assistant text for github-copilot/claude-* models
alta.titulo_traduzido: (#27697) regression in v1.14.50: `TeamCode run --format json` drops post-tool-call assistant text for github-copilot/claude-* models
alta.descricao_original:
> From anomalyco/teamcode#27697

## Summary

In teamcode **v1.14.50**, `teamcode run --format json --model github-copilot/claude-* "<prompt that triggers a tool call>"` exits cleanly (rc=0) but **never emits the assistant text turn that follows the tool call**. Stdout contains the first `step_start` / `tool_use` / `tool` / `step_finish (reason: tool-calls)`, then a second `step_start`, then **nothing** — no `text`, no second `step_finish`.

The same prompt on **v1.14.48** emits 2 `text` events and a final `step_finish (reason: stop)`. The same prompt on v1.14.50 against `github-copilot/gpt-5.4` (or any non-Claude provider I tested) also works correctly. Single-turn prompts (no tool call) on Claude+v1.14.50 also work — only the **multi-step / post-tool-call** turn is dropped.

This breaks every headless integration that relies on `--format json` to capture Claude responses involving any tool use (read, bash, etc.) — output is silently truncated to zero text content with no error.

## Af
